Fixing P and S, let v=x+z∈[2√P,S], then x=(v+√(v²-4P))/2 and y=S-v. Squared operator norm max(x,y) is max of increasing and decreasing branches, yielding exact L/U endpoints with transition S=3√P. The Schatten-fourth power x²+y²+z²=v²-2P+(S-v)² is convex, so its minimum crosses at S=4√P and maximum is endpoint v=S; continuity fills intervals. Reduce universal squared norm ratio U/L to r=S/√P; monotonicity makes unique maximum at r=3 equal φ². Fourth-Schatten power ratio maximizes at r=2+√2 with value 1+√2. Explicit valid squared weights attain both. Independent exact 4x4 determinant expansion and branch optimization tests succeeded. Boundary S=2√P, b=0 included.
